standard_prerequisites.name: Models of a curve, semistable reduction and the three genus cases
standard_prerequisites.statement: A model of a smooth projective curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring is a flat proper scheme over the ring with that curve as generic fibre, and its reduction is semistable when the special fibre is nodal; after a finite separable extension of the base one may pass to the integral closure and consider models over its localisations. The chapter treats the three genus cases in three separate sections, proving that a curve of genus zero becomes the projective line after a quadratic separable extension, that a curve of genus one acquires semistable reduction whose special fibre is controlled by the minimal model, and that a curve of genus at least two acquires semistable reduction after a finite separable extension, the last case using the fact that torsion in the Picard group of the model becomes visible after such an extension. The author's own sections and the quoted result of the Curves chapter are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem is the main result of the chapter: it is the semistable reduction statement that the chapter's preceding sections are built to prove, and its proof is the assembly of those sections.

core_obligations: State the three genus cases: the theorem collects the conclusions of the chapter's three sections on curves of genus zero, one and at least two, each of which produces a finite separable extension of the base over which the curve has semistable reduction (source lines 6888-6892).

Genus zero: the section on genus zero supplies a quadratic separable extension over which the curve becomes isomorphic to the projective line, which is the first enumerated case (source lines 6892-6894).

Genus one: the section on genus one supplies a finite separable extension over which the curve has semistable reduction over every localisation of the integral closure, with the special fibre of the minimal model described, which is the second case; the action of the Galois group on the reduction is controlled there as well (source lines 6894-6898).

Genus at least two: the section on the remaining case supplies a finite separable extension over which the curve has semistable reduction, using that torsion in the Picard group becomes visible after such an extension, which is the third case and completes the theorem (source lines 6898-6900).

proof_roadmap.step: Collect the three genus cases from the chapter's three sections.
Genus zero: the curve becomes the projective line after a quadratic separable extension.
Genus one: semistable reduction over every localisation, with the minimal model's special fibre described.
Genus at least two: semistable reduction after a finite separable extension, via visible torsion.
